title.en: Define sin x and cos x on the unit circle
Find the signs in each quadrant
Find all six functions from one

say.en: A right triangle cannot hold an angle of 200 degrees, yet a Ferris wheel turns through it every ride. The unit circle can. In this lesson: Define sin x and cos x on the unit circle.
Find the signs in each quadrant.
Find all six functions from one.

body.en: Let the arc of length $x$ on the unit circle from $(1, 0)$ end at $P(a, b)$. Then $\cos x = a$ and $\sin x = b$. So $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$. The other *functions* are $\tan x = \sin x/\cos x$, $\cot x = \cos x/\sin x$, $\sec x = 1/\cos x$, $\csc x = 1/\sin x$. Also $1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x$ and $1 + \cot^2 x = \csc^2 x$.
body.kn: ಏಕಮಾನ ವೃತ್ತದ ಮೇಲಿನ ಬಿಂದು P(a, b) ಗೆ cos x = a, sin x = b. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ sin²x + cos²x = 1.

narration.en: On the unit circle, cos x is the x-coordinate and sin x is the y-coordinate of the point reached. So sine squared plus cosine squared is always one.
narration.kn: ಏಕಮಾನ ವೃತ್ತದ ಮೇಲಿನ ಬಿಂದು P(a, b) ಗೆ cos x = a, sin x = b. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ sin²x + cos²x = 1.

body.en: sin and cos repeat every $2\pi$: $\sin(2n\pi + x) = \sin x$, $\cos(2n\pi + x) = \cos x$. Also $\sin(-x) = -\sin x$, $\cos(-x) = \cos x$. *Signs*: quadrant I all positive; II only sin and cosec; III only tan and cot; IV only cos and sec.

heading.en: Angles, Radian Measure and Trigonometric Functions

tagline.en: Degree and radian measure, l = rθ, trigonometric functions of any real number through the unit circle, standard values and signs in the four quadrants.

myth.en: For an arc subtending $60^\circ$ in a circle of radius 6 cm, $l = r\theta = 6 \times 60 = 360$ cm.

truth.en: Convert first: $60^\circ = \frac{\pi}{3}$ rad, so $l = 6 \times \frac{\pi}{3} = 2\pi \approx 6.28$ cm. The formula l = rθ comes from the definition of the radian, so it is false for degrees. A quick sense check: an arc can never be longer than the whole circumference (here about 37.7 cm).

say.en: $\pi$ radians $= 180^\circ$; $l = r\theta$ needs $\theta$ in radians.
On the unit circle, the point at arc length $x$ from $(1, 0)$ is $(\cos x, \sin x)$, for every real $x$.
$\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$, $1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x$, $1 + \cot^2 x = \operatorname{cosec}^2 x$.
Positive functions by quadrant: I all, II sin, III tan, IV cos (with their reciprocals).
$\sin x = 0 \iff x = n\pi$; $\cos x = 0 \iff x = (2n + 1)\frac{\pi}{2}$.

problem.en: cos x = −3/5 and x lies in the third quadrant. Find the other five trigonometric functions.

steps.en: sin²x = 1 − 9/25 = 16/25; in quadrant III sin x = −4/5.

answer.en: sin x = −4/5, tan x = 4/3, cot x = 3/4, sec x = −5/3, cosec x = −5/4

narration.en: Let us solve this together. cos x = −3/5 and x lies in the third quadrant. Find the other five trigonometric functions.

say.en: Let us solve this together. cos x equals minus 3 over 5 and x lies in the third quadrant. Find the other five trigonometric functions.
sin squaredx equals 1 minus 9 over 25 equals 16 over 25; in quadrant III sin x equals minus 4 over 5.
tan x equals 4 over 3, cot x equals 3 over 4.
sec x equals minus 5 over 3, cosec x equals minus 5 over 4.
So the answer is sin x equals minus 4 over 5, tan x equals 4 over 3, cot x equals 3 over 4, sec x equals minus 5 over 3, cosec x equals minus 5 over 4.

steps.en: 31π/3 = 10π + π/3, and 10π is five full turns.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find sin(31π/3).

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find sin(31 pi /3).
31 pi /3 equals 10 pi plus pi /3, and 10 pi is five full turns.
sin(31 pi /3) equals sin(pi /3) equals the square root of 3 over 2.
So the answer is the square root of 3 over 2.
